neighbours.label: the token just before a word of likeness or 'other' in a comparison between two groups (which are (similar), together with (other)): a predictor of similar/other/analogous
fire: Wolves can breed with domestic dogs, which are similar in size and build.
The Welsh miners joined forces with workers in other regions to demand higher pay.
Mules are often compared to hinnies, which are similar but smaller.
Teachers in Ohio met together with teachers from other states in Chicago.
Lemons can be crossed with limes, which are similar in taste and colour.
The farmers of the valley united with farmers in other provinces against the tax.
Crows are closely related to ravens, which are similar in behaviour.
The Polish refugees settled together with refugees from other countries in the camp.
quiet: Wolves can travel for miles at night, which makes them hard to track.
The Welsh miners worked long shifts underground to earn a living.
Mules are often used on farms, which makes them valuable to farmers.
Teachers in Ohio met on Monday to plan the school year.
Lemons can be stored in the fridge, which keeps them fresh for weeks.
The farmers of the valley sold their wheat at the market every week.
Crows are often seen in parks, where they look for food.
The Polish refugees settled near the river and built small houses.
